findings.evidence: Both statements mention only Mathlib types C(X, ℝ), and their proofs use only convexity, pointwise inequalities, and the uniform metric; neither depends on summing operators.
findings.fix: Move both to a general continuous-map module and export them.
findings.issue: convex_uniformlyPositive and isOpen_uniformlyPositive (line 207) are reusable infrastructure hidden inside the Pietsch proof.

findings.evidence: The @[simp] theorem evalRpow_apply at lines 43–45 already characterizes evaluation; Pietsch uses .continuous at line 86 and evalRpow_apply at line 305.
findings.fix: Remove @[expose]; use evalRpow_apply for evaluation and its continuous projection for continuity, adding characteristic lemmas if further consumers need them.
findings.issue: @[expose] unnecessarily makes evalRpow's implementation part of the public interface.

summary: Two general continuous-function results are hidden as private helpers, and evalRpow unnecessarily exposes its body.
